placements.why: The envelope's content is a ratified design contract for the memory/extraction pipeline's async job mechanics (receipt, cursor, dispatch-then-poll) — an organizational-strategy category of its own (how the system is built), distinct from opportunity, product, or proof concerns. Nothing in the supplied strata (empty) or graph structure covers this, and 'Architecture' is the exact, standard name for this kind of content per the org's known taxonomy shape, so it is minted fresh rather than folded under an unrelated or absent category.
placements.title: System design contracts as the organizing category

placements.title: Remember becomes a dispatch that returns a receipt, not a call that blocks for a result
placements.frame: What does the async job contract guarantee about latency and durability, and how does the agent retrieve the eventual result — polling, piggybacking, or some new mechanism — across future envelopes?
placements.why: All three expressions describe one recurring, future-feeding subject — the shape of the async job contract itself: src-1 states the receipt-and-cursor mechanics, src-2 states the guarantees those mechanics buy (non-blocking, no lost work), and src-3 names the dispatch-then-poll-or-piggyback retrieval pattern as the 'key decision.' This is a design theme, not a one-time fact — future envelopes will keep describing how agents fulfill or extend this contract (new retrieval paths, failure modes, guarantee changes), which is exactly the narrative grain test. No existing leaf or hub was available to reuse (graph structure supplied is empty), so this is minted fresh under the newly-minted Architecture strata rather than left standalone, since it is squarely a system-design subject.
